clauses.text: The review host binds to 127.0.0.1 and serves only the shell, the bootstrap script, the two packaged UI files and the review API; the journal root resolves from --journal, then BRAINBASE_JUDGMENT_JOURNAL_DIR, then the default.
An unavailable journal or a malformed response is never rendered as zero items; the home shows three sections and the recording coverage including a possible stall.

The judgment card shows handling, decision, work impact, basis, recorded basis target (entity ID and optional version), prior learning reuse, execution, outcome and feedback in that order. A recorded basis target is visible for traceability; a missing target remains explicit and no source link is invented.

Saving feedback requires the per-process token and same origin, rejects decisions absent from the journal, requires a reason for corrected and reverted, confirms the saved value by reloading, and keeps the draft on failure.
The consult action copies a request text that includes the decision attempt ID.

The review host rejects every request, including the shell, the review API and feedback, unless the Host header is 127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1] with the port the connection arrived on, so a rebound DNS name cannot read the token or judgments or write feedback.

The value-proof-review UI part lets a host that cannot read a local journal replace the unavailable notice title and guidance; the notice still shows the reason and never renders as zero items, and the default guidance stays the local --journal and environment variable hint.

The possible-stall notice is explicitly scoped to web-readable .value-proof.json value-confirmation records, explains that the judgment journal also writes other episode/final records, and does not claim that the whole judgment journal stopped or infer its latest write status from this notice; unavailable or unconfirmed counts and timestamps remain neither zero nor success.

When the local journal is unavailable, the default notice gives concrete --journal and BRAINBASE_JUDGMENT_JOURNAL_DIR setup steps and a visible retry action; a host-provided notice keeps its own guidance and still offers retry without adding local-only instructions.

The value-proof payload currently has no source URL or source-read contract. The UI must not fabricate a navigable source; adding source navigation requires a separately defined contract and an actual target fixture.
